findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe action is exposed as a GET request
findings.body: `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` changes a user's notification level, and this action is explicitly exempted from the XHR check. Because GET requests do not receive Rails CSRF protection, any page or email/link scanner that causes a logged-in user's browser to request this URL can change that user's topic subscription without their intent. This can also be triggered by browser prefetching or security scanners following the emailed link. Make the email link lead to a confirmation page and perform the mutation via a CSRF-protected POST/PUT request (or use a signed, single-purpose token if a one-click email unsubscribe is required).

findings.title: Unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change, so automatic tracking can re-enable notifications
findings.body: The action directly assigns and saves `notification_level` rather than using `TopicUser.change`. `TopicUser.change` records `notifications_changed_at` and, crucially, sets `notifications_reason_id` to `user_changed`. The automatic tracking logic treats a nil reason as eligible to promote a topic back to `tracking` after it is read. Thus a topic user record with no reason (the normal case for auto-tracked topics) can be muted through this endpoint and later automatically changed back to tracking when the user visits/reads it, undoing the unsubscribe. Route this update through `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` so the explicit user choice is persisted with the appropriate reason and timestamp.
